In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the cholestyramines increased the DMH-induced enteric carcinogenesis, probably through the increased absorption of bile acids.
cholestyramines, by increasing the frequency of DM-H-induced intestinal neoplasia, may be considered to be a promoting agent.
DMH-induced carcinogenesis in germfree rats is promoted by cholestyramin.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
DMH-induced carcinogenesis in the rat colon is associated with the bile acid metabolism, and cholestyramines may be useful in the chemoprevention of DMH-induced carcinomas in germfree rats.
the carcinogenicity of DMH in germfree animals may be enhanced by a supplement of cholestyramin.
cholestyramin-induced enteric carcinogenesis in germfree rats was associated with a significant increase in the concentration of total bile acids in the cecum, especially in the lithocholic acid.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the bile acid metabolism is altered by cholestyramines in germfree rats, and that this alteration may contribute to the carcinogenesis.
the bile acid metabolism is closely associated with the enteric carcinogenisis.
cholestyramin can be used to increase the frequency of enteric carcinogenesis and that the bile acid metabolism may be a key factor for this effect.
